Block Listing Application
An application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for a block listing of 400,000
new ordinary shares of 3.5p in the Company ("New Ordinary Shares") to be admitted to the Official List and to trading on the London Stock Exchange. The admission is expected to be effective on 28 August 2026. 200,000 New Ordinary Shares will be used to satisfy the allotment of shares pursuant to the vesting of awards from time to time under ASOS Plc Long-Term Incentive Scheme ("ALTIS") and 200,000 New Ordinary Shares will be used to satisfy the allotment of shares pursuant to the vesting of options from time to time under the ASOS Plc Sharesave Plan.
The New Ordinary Shares will be issued fully paid and will rank pari passu in all respects with the existing issued Ordinary Shares of the Company.

latest.title: Disposal of Atlanta fulfilment centre
latest.content:
1 Jul 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 4790K
ASOS PLC
01 July 2026
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION
1 July 2026
ASOS Plc
Global Online Fashion Destination
"ASOS" or the "Group"
Disposal of Atlanta fulfilment centre for c.£48m;marks completion of non-core asset sale programme
ASOS today announces that it has signed and completed the assignment of the lease of its Atlanta fulfilment centre and the disposal of the associated automation assets (together, the "Transaction"). The lease has been assigned to a global consumer brand and the assets are being purchased by a member of the DHL Group. The Transaction marks a further strengthening of the Group's financial position, with net proceeds of c.£48m (c.$63m) and annual cash cost savings of c.£6m at current exchange rates (c.$8m).
Strategic Rationale: Continued execution of ASOS's Efficient Operating Model
The disposal of the Atlanta fulfilment centre represents a further step in ASOS's programme to strengthen its balance sheet and deliver disciplined capital allocation. The site is non-operational and was fully written down in prior periods, and the Transaction enables the Group to realise value from a non-core asset while continuing to simplify its asset base and improve cash generation.
This disposal builds on a series of actions to improve the Group's financial position, including the refinancing in November 2025, repayment of the 2026 convertible bonds in April 2026 and the disposal of the Lichfield fulfilment centre in May 2026. Net proceeds will be retained to support financial flexibility as ASOS continues to execute its strategy.
Financial Impact
The Transaction has resulted in net sale proceeds of c.£48m, with annual cash savings of c.£6m relating to rent and other occupancy costs. There is also a one-off profit before tax of c.£78m at current exchange rates (c.$103m) after adjustments to associated property liabilities which will be recognised as an adjusting item in the Group's financial results for FY26.
The net proceeds will add to the Group's cash position of £209.5m as at 1 March 2026. Taking into account the c.£67m net proceeds from the disposal of the Lichfield fulfilment centre and the c.£48m net proceeds from the Atlanta Transaction, the pro forma net debt (excluding lease liabilities) position is c.£180m (net debt was c.£295m as at 1 March 2026).
Jose Antonio Ramos, ASOS CEO, said:
"The disposal of Atlanta is another clear demonstration of us delivering on our commitments - strengthening the balance sheet, simplifying the business and maintaining strict discipline in how we allocate capital. Since closing the Atlanta fulfilment centre, we have successfully transitioned to our new US operating model, giving customers access to a broader product assortment from our global inventory. The strength of customer engagement gives us confidence in this approach and reinforces the progress we are making as we execute our strategy and reposition ASOS for long-term, sustainable growth."
The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Rishi Sharma, General Counsel and Company Secretary.

latest.content:

ASOS PLC
09 June 2026
9 June 2026
ASOS Plc
("ASOS" or the "Company")
Director Notification
Christine Cross, Independent Non-Executive Director, has informed the Board of her intention not to seek re-election at the next Annual General Meeting ("AGM") of the Company, which is expected to be held in early 2027, in order to focus on other personal and professional commitments.
Christine has served as Chair of the Remuneration Committee and as a member of the Audit Committee since her appointment in April 2024. ASOS is following its succession planning process to recruit an Independent Non-Executive Director to Chair the Remuneration Committee and the Company will announce the successor in due course.
Natasja Laheij, ASOS Chair, said:
"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Christine for her significant contribution to the Company during her tenure. She has played an important role in re-shaping the Company's Executive Remuneration and has been a valued member of the Board. We respect Christine's decision not to seek re-election and wish her all the best for the future".
Christine Cross, Independent Non-Executive Director, said:
"It has been a privilege to serve on the Board of ASOS. I am proud of what we have achieved during my time with the Company and wish the Board and management continued success".

company_30s.what_they_do: ASC.L is a small‑cap listed company that operates a network of fulfilment and logistics hubs for e‑commerce retailers.  It handles warehousing, inventory management and last‑mile delivery for a mix of mid‑market brands.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits on the back‑end of the online retail boom.  Its hubs support the same merchants that power major shopping platforms, giving it a built‑in client base and a recurring revenue stream that can scale with the growth of e‑commerce.
company_30s.current_state: ASC.L is in a restructuring phase – it has sold an Atlanta fulfilment centre, filed for a block listing and is tightening its balance sheet.  The company is still trading in the penny range and is under heavy scrutiny from shareholders, but it is actively trimming costs and positioning itself for a leaner operation.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy with corporate governance moves – a block listing application, changes in director holdings, and a notice of results.  These steps signal a desire to clean up the board and reduce regulatory friction.

Financially, ASC.L has just released interim results, a refinancing announcement and a disposal of a non‑core asset.  The refinancing indicates that the firm is still able to access capital markets, while the asset sale shows a willingness to shed excess capacity.

The overarching theme is a shift from a sprawling operation to a focused, cost‑efficient logistics provider.  If the company can keep the cost base lean while keeping its client contracts intact, the market may start to see value again.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Bullish optimism about a post‑results rebound
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Several community members are confident the company will hit the £4.50 target after the next earnings release, citing improved cash flow and a clearer strategy.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some traders warn that the stock is still too volatile and that a further dilution or a failed refinancing could push the price back to pennies.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has been steady, with a few bullish posts but no major sell‑off.  The mood is cautiously optimistic but still tentative.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for ASC.L is flat, meaning no one is actively searching for the ticker.  This lack of public interest is a classic contrarian signal – the market is sleeping on a potential upside.

near_term_catalysts: Upcoming earnings release – the company is scheduled to report full results in late September.  A better‑than‑expected profit or a clear guidance lift would be the most direct trigger.
Completion of the Atlanta hub sale – the proceeds could be used to pay down debt or fund new contracts, creating a positive headline.
Potential refinancing or new credit line – if the company can secure a more favourable debt package, it would signal confidence from lenders.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a breakout above the recent low (around the current penny level) accompanied by a surge in volume.  A sustained rise above the 20‑day moving average would confirm a reversal.  Also keep an eye on any new contracts announced by the company’s sales team.
expect_next.timing_regime: The APEX score is high, suggesting a tight compression.  If the price has already capitulated to the low end of its range, the next move is likely to be a sharp rebound.  The company’s restructuring indicates that it may be at the tail end of the crash phase, but it still needs a clear catalyst to trigger mean reversion.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is trading in the penny range, while community chatter points to a £4.50 target.  If the company can deliver a solid earnings beat, the upside is multi‑hundred percent.  Even a recovery to 50% of that target would deliver a 10‑to‑1 reward for the risk taken.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company’s current capital structure is fragile – a failed refinancing or a new round of dilution could push the price back to zero.  There is also the risk that the asset sale does not cover the debt, leaving shareholders with a paper loss.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 10‑to‑1 or higher if the price reaches the £4.50 level.  Potential downside: complete loss of the invested capital if the company collapses or is delisted.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 20‑day SMA with a stop just below the recent low.  Use a 5% portfolio allocation and trail the stop by 20% of the price once the trade is in profit.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for the earnings release.  If the company posts a positive surprise, look for a volume spike and a price break above the 20‑day SMA before committing.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy signals at this time.

ai_insights.bottom_line: ASC.L is a penny‑trading logistics firm that has undergone significant restructuring.  With a flat Google trend signal and a bullish community mood around a £4.50 target, the contrarian thesis hinges on a positive earnings release and a successful asset sale.  The upside is substantial, but the risk of a total collapse remains if the company cannot secure fresh capital.
